    The news that Tesla(TSLA -7.64%)is inviting select customers to buy Cybercabs isn't a game changer from a financial perspective (at least not immediately). Still, it is highly symbolic and highlights the case for Tesla shareholders holding fire on agreeing to a potential merger with Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) (or SpaceX for short). Here's why.

    Recent findings suggest that in itself, buying a Cybercab right now is hardly an attractive option for most people. They are reported to cost $29,990, but they can't be used without a $299 monthly subscription, they lack manual driving controls (a steering wheel, pedals, etc.), and they can only operate in the limited geo-fenced areas where the robotaxi service currently operates.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    However, they will obviously attract Tesla enthusiasts, social media influencers, and those confident in widespread regulatory approvals for Tesla's robotaxi service. To be clear, as management is, it's focused on becoming a transportation-as-a-service company with the "vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned and Transport-as-a-Service," according to CEO Elon Musk.

    The reality is their sale is more about generating promotional buzz around robotaxis as the company prepares for a widespread expansion in 2027. Fortunately, everything points to a quantum leap in the robotaxi rollout next year. The company continues to develop its next major upgrade of its full self-driving software, namely v15, which should be validated and released by early 2027.

    Also, Cybercab production is ramping up, and Tesla notes it's gathering data on unsupervised miles with its robotaxi at a double-digit weekly growth rate.

    In a recent development, after years of delays and missed timelines, everything points to Tesla finally releasing value from its robotaxi service next year. At which point, its investors are entitled to ask whether it would make sense to agree to a merger with SpaceX before the robotaxi ramps up.

    While an offer is not on the table, and investors don't know the terms of a deal, or whether there will even be one, it's hard not to think that a robotaxi ramp-up in 2027 would increase Tesla's share price.

    As such, if you believe Tesla is undervalued right now, then anything other than a significant cash premium from SpaceX would make sense. The following table outlines the matter from a Tesla shareholder's perspective. If you are in conditions A or B (a highly unlikely scenario), you don't want to sell undervalued Tesla stock at a discount. Investors shouldn't hold Tesla stock if they believe it's overvalued, as in C and D.

    Data source: Author's analysis.

    The only caveat to this table is that investors believe a united firm -- SpaceX's artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure combined with Tesla's physical AI -- would be much stronger than the sum of its parts. That argument holds merit, but it holds even more merit after te automaker successfully ramps up its robotaxi and develops the Cybercab service. The company would be in a stronger negotiating position then, and the Cybercab sales launch helps underline how close the company is to getting there.

    A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

    Should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

    Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

    For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

    While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any massive moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

    Industry observers note that that’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he claims. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

    Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

    If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

    For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a latest policy in the health insurance marketplace.

    Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your newly introduced job search — is also an important part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

    Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty states.

    “Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

    You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

    At the same time, it’s notable to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage company, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

    Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

    In a recent development, it’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a new park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

    “Having that release is mentally a big thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

    Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, says Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

    People often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she claims.

    Industry observers note that starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine claims. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

    Doing something fresh also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so blueprint accordingly.

    All three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

    Sources indicate that the Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

    Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    • Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.
    • Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's initiative to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S.
    • "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's initiative to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio said. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    It has been revealed that bessent noted in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    Recent findings suggest that after years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    In a recent development, to solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    In a recent development, first, Dalio mentioned the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Latest York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio mentioned. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he said.

    Dalio said it's key to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    In a recent development, dalio said the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder mentioned.

    According to recent reports, dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (780 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
    • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
    • A mortgage is a massive ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

    The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

    A mortgage is a massive ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

    Sources indicate that one bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

    Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

    Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) revealed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

    In a recent development, while CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

    Industry observers note that to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

    Even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how promptly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

    According to recent reports, if you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

    But new data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

    Pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

    “Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun remarked in a news release.

    According to recent reports, whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

    Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

    Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

    Industry observers note that think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

    Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

    10 stocks we like better than Home Depot ›.

    In a recent development, about nine months ago in mid-February, the average 30-year fixed rate mortgage was at 6.09%. At that time, it was much higher compared to what consumers saw from 2009 to 2022. Things have only gotten tighter throughout this year.

    It has been revealed that today, the 30-year fixed rate mortgage is at 7.11%. It has moved up more than one percentage point in roughly nine months. Outside of the past four years, it hasn't been this elevated since 2002. On a $500,000 house, the difference between 7.11% and 6.09% translates to hundreds of dollars more in monthly payments.

    Recent findings suggest that in October, existing housing sales dipped to their lowest level in 16 years. This is a frozen market. And shareholders in Home Depot (HD +0.70%) and Lowe's (LOW +0.78%) are feeling the pain.

    Deciding to tackle a home renovation, upgrade, or repair is no small undertaking. It can be a sizable capital commitment for people. Anytime consumers deal with big purchases, the companies involved are exposed to fluctuating demand. Unlike buying products or services on a recurring schedule, these households can choose to delay these projects.

    With the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage above 7%, Home Depot and Lowe's are in a bind. "Housing turnover hasn't moved in four years now," incoming Home Depot chief executive officer (and current chief financial officer) Richard McPhail said on the Q3 2026 earnings call.

    It has been revealed that less activity in the housing market means fewer people are moving. On the flip side, when more people are changing homes, it can naturally lead to higher demand for the things that Home Depot and Lowe's sell.

    In a recent development, during its fiscal 2026 third quarter (ended Nov. 1), Home Depot, which is the clear leader in the industry, posted a 0.5% decline in comparable transactions. Lowe's fared worse. It reported that this figure fell by 1.7%.

    Industry observers note that transaction counts are a proxy for foot traffic. When it comes to any retailer, investors want to see this metric growing.

    It has been revealed that same-store sales (SSS), however, grew for both companies thanks to the impact of higher average ticket sizes. Both of these leadership teams called out appliances as a strong product category, pushing substantial-ticket comp sales up mid-single digits.

    It doesn't look like these companies will get any relief soon on the macro front. According to CME Group's (CME +0.41%) FedWatch, trading activity suggests that there's a 100% probability the fed funds rate will be higher after the December meeting, up from the current range of 3.75% to 4%. The problem is inflation that's lingering longer than expected.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    For what it's worth, Home Depot and Lowe's do expect SSS to be positive for fiscal 2026. And both are finding that demand from their professional customer bases, which consist of contractors, plumbers, electricians, and the like, is stronger than spending from DIY consumers. These companies are getting better at serving their professionals, enhancing areas like fulfillment, customer service, and loyalty programs.

    According to recent reports, past investments in supply chain and omnichannel capabilities are also paying off. Home Depot's online comparable sales jumped 13% in the third quarter. Lowe's saw a 17% gain. Their scale, supported by massive revenue bases, give them the ability to bolster their operations, which is something smaller rivals can't do.

    A housing market recovery could take time, but there appears to be meaningful pent-up demand. Accessible home equity is at a record $13 trillion.

    Investors in these two retail stocks will still have to stay extremely patient, as they have been in recent years. Shares in Home Depot and Lowe's put up total returns of 19% and 16%, respectively, in the past three years. That's worse than the 69% total return of the S&P 500 index(^GSPC -3.70%).

    As long as SSS remain under pressure for these businesses, reporting strong earnings growth is out of the question. Usually a notable tailwind, it won't play much of a factor in portfolios.

    It has been revealed that on a positive note, Home Depot and Lowe's are quality companies that are on solid financial footing. They can weather the storm. Investors have to figure out, however, if they're willing to wait for the situation to improve.

    The biggest volatility came following the November 3rd midterm elections, and it has a lot of people wondering whether now is the time to get a bit more defensive heading into 2027.

    But history suggests that this is the time to buy. In fact, it's one of the strongest track records out there.

    It has been revealed that since 1970, there have been 14 midterm elections, defined as the halfway point of the 4-year presidential term. And in each one of those midterms, the S&P 500 has been higher both 6 months later and one year later all 14 times.

    It has been revealed that the returns for stocks have been fantastic during these periods too. The median 6-month gain post-midterm was 12.6%, more than triple that of the 4% median return during non-midterm years.

    According to recent reports, over the full subsequent year, the outperformance is a little more muted. Midterm years have seen a median gain of about 11% compared to 10% in other years.

    What's also impressive is that these post-midterm rallies occurred even during years when it looked like conditions wouldn't favor it. In 1974, for example, the S&P 500 was down 23% for the year at this point and rallied 21% over the next six months. In 2022, the index was in a bear market, down 16%, and still gained 3.3% over the next six months and 10.6% over the next year.

    Recent findings suggest that data source: Investing.com and the author's analysis of S&P 500 daily closing prices. Each starting point is the final close of the week ending between Nov. 7 and Nov. 13. Six months = 26 weeks; 12 months = 52 weeks.

    Admittedly, this is a small sample size so we don't want to put too much weight into these conclusions.

    In the 2000s, the midterm outperformance trend has weakened considerably. While it's still maintaining its perfect record of gains, the S&P 500's performance has been pretty average overall. In most cases, the markets saw an immediate boost once the uncertainty over the election results was lifted. But beyond that, the market in recent years hasn't gotten much of an extended boost.

    As of November 17, the S&P 500 is down around 3% since election day but still up about 7% on the year as a whole.

    The substantial question facing the markets right now is what's going to happen with artificial intelligence (AI)? Heavy spending in AI development is being viewed negatively; there could be a significant slowdown in data center development; and worries are growing that red-hot earnings growth rates are ready to slow.

    Above average inflation, high interest rates, and the potential for multiple Fed rate hikes over the next several quarters could also pose headwinds.

    Earnings growth for the S&P 500 is still expected to be solid, but there are any number of factors that could, over the next 12 months, derail the narrative.

    The high degree of uncertainty looking forward over the next few quarters helps make the case for a long-term view.

    History is on the side of the S&P 500 here, but investor confidence has been shaken over the past month, and the number of potential stumbling blocks is getting massive. This could very well be the year the post-midterm bounce trend doesn't hold.

    In a recent development, since the markets could move in either direction, the best idea is probably to just stay put. Don't try to time the market and bet which way stock prices will move. Just keep contributing to your accounts and maintain a focus on your goals further down the road instead.

    Industry News: This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • Sources indicate that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that hilton is making a major play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    Sources indicate that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    It has been revealed that hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    Industry observers note that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    For cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Recent findings suggest that stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    It has been revealed that there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    Recent findings suggest that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    Industry observers note that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    It has been revealed that if you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    AMD Stock Just Plunged on a Short-Seller Report. Is This a Golden Buying Opportunity?

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:30AM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.
    • It has been revealed that chip stocks can't seem to catch a break.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:30AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

    It has been revealed that chip stocks can't seem to catch a break. Recent developments, including a scandal and a major leadership change at Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), the most notable semiconductor tech giant, have weighed on the industry.

    Sources indicate that another market leader is now facing a headwind. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) was the target of a short-seller report published on Nov. 19, which sent the tech giant's shares down significantly, extending the losses the chipmaker had experienced over the past few weeks. Is AMD worth investing in on the dip?

    In a recent development, hunterbrook Media, an investigative journalism outlet, published the report in question. It is affiliated with Hunterbrook Capital, a hedge fund that trades based on reporting from its journalism arm.

    Recent findings suggest that in the report, Hunterbrook claims that some of AMD's firmware ended up in the hands of a Chinese server manufacturer that the U.S. government has blacklisted. That means AMD cannot sell its software to this tech giant, at least not without the appropriate license or authorization, and may be in violation of export restrictions if it does so.

    If AMD is found to have broken the law, it could face penalties, including a hefty fine, more stringent export restrictions, or, worse, criminal investigations involving its executives. This could disrupt the organization's business for a while.

    Sources indicate that but that's if the allegations are true. Hunterbrook itself acknowledges that it doesn't know how this Chinese tech giant got hold of AMD's firmware. It could have obtained the firmware in various ways that do not involve the company that made it.

    Recent findings suggest that there's also the possibility that AMD does have the appropriate export license. At any rate, there is limited direct evidence that demonstrates wrongdoing on the part of AMD, at least in my view.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that it's worth noting that AMD has denied these allegations. That's what the company would do, of course. It wouldn't simply acknowledge wrongdoing publicly. However, Hunterbrook Capital itself stands to gain from a decline in AMD's stock price.

    That's how short-sellers make money. So there is also a financial incentive. Meanwhile, Reuters, a highly respected journalism outlet, said that it could not independently verify Hunterbrook's claims. That doesn't mean the claims are false.

    But the evidence for them is looking slim, at best. In my view, investors should ignore this whole debacle and continue focusing on AMD's fundamentals and business outlook. And once we do that, there is a strong case for investing in AMD.

    Consider the manufacturer's third-quarter results. AMD's revenue increased by 45% year over year to $13.4 billion. The company's non-GAAP gross margin was 56%, up from 54% in the year-ago period, while it posted non-GAAP earnings per share of $2.09, up 74% from the prior-year quarter.

    AMD's data center segment was once again the star of the show, with its sales nearly doubling to a record $8.5 billion. Business is booming for AMD, and there is more where that came from. The tech giant's leadership in CPUs (central processing units) positions it well to capitalize on the growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) agents.

    Recent findings suggest that agentic AI runs on CPUs, and this market is driving up AMD's sales. As management noted, data center revenue growth has accelerated every quarter this year, and that should continue in the fourth quarter, thanks in part to the ongoing agentic AI boom. AMD expects revenue growth of more than 80% in 2027, well above the growth it posted in 2026.

    And over the next five years, we could see the semiconductor leader continue to tap into its large server CPU total addressable market (TAM), which should reach $220 billion by 2030, according to the manufacturer's projections -- and AMD has increased its mid-term TAM estimates several times over the past year as demand for its products continues to expand.

    It has been revealed that the opportunity across the entire range of its business is even larger. Lastly, AMD is trading at 31.4x forward earnings, a fair valuation, in my view, considering the opportunities ahead. The stock may not stay down for too long. Investors should buy the dip.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

    Sources indicate that there are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    They’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    In a recent development, you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

    Each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    Industry observers note that new lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    In a recent development, global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

    Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

    If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

    If you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

    This community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Recent findings suggest that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    This community would be an excellent choice if your upcoming travels include several of these airports, even if dining isn't the main reason for your trips. If dining out is one of your favorite activities, check out the best credit cards for restaurants.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:.

    Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, these destinations qualify for bonus points and status points:.

    This community may be especially valuable if you regularly book award flights for children 12 and under. Even if you don't travel with kids, it could be worth considering if its qualifying airports align better with your travel aims than those of other communities.

    Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:.

    Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

    Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

    Two Travel Now discounts per year for 30% off one-way refundable Y-class fares on Alaska Airlines, booked within four days of departure for travel to, from or within Alaska.

    Ship cargo within Alaska for $49 plus tax (weight, size and content limits apply).

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    In a recent development, baggage benefits don’t combine with other free checked bag allowances, such as those that come with some Alaska credit cards. However, they apply to everyone traveling on the same reservation.

    It has been revealed that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus offers:.

    It has been revealed that while this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel plans — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

    Hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:.

    Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

    Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

    Earn 50% more points and status points on flights between Hawaiian islands beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

    • In a recent development, microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) hit a record close of $555.80 on Nov.
    • Recent findings suggest that part of that drop comes from the broader market.
    • In a recent development, A fast drop from a newly introduced peak can feel like a warning.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 3:41AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Microsoft ›.

    In a recent development, microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) hit a record close of $555.80 on Nov. 4. Nine trading days later, on Nov. 17, it ended at $506.24 -- around 9% under the high. Shares trade near $508 as of this writing.

    Recent findings suggest that part of that drop comes from the broader market. The Nasdaq-100 fell around 5% in the same stretch. But Microsoft fell more.

    In a recent development, A fast drop from a newly introduced peak can feel like a warning. For Microsoft, it usually hasn't been one.

    In a recent development, by my count of its daily closes, the stock has fallen this fast from a record on 18 past occasions since 1995. Shares were higher 12 months later in 15 of the cases, and the typical (median) gain was around 30%. That's about twice the median one-year gain of about 15% for all trading days in the same stretch.

    It has been revealed that every case begins on the first day Microsoft closed at least 8% under a record close set within the past 15 trading days. I used split-adjusted closing prices without dividends and counted just one case per record, so a stock that kept falling couldn't count twice until it hit a upcoming high.

    "A year later" means the close 12 months after that first 8% day.

    Recent findings suggest that the recent record is especially strong. Since 2018, Microsoft has done this nine times, and the stock was higher a year later in all nine. The middle result was a rise of around 29%.

    The best one came in September 2020, when shares rose about 48% over the next year.

    But the ride was rarely smooth. Ten of the 18 saw shares fall at least another 10% before the year ended.

    Sources indicate that the latest case highlights how rough that can be. Once the stock slid 8% under its Oct. 28, 2025, record, it eventually closed around 29% below where it stood on that 8% day. It didn't hit a newly introduced record until Oct. 13, 2026. And a year after the pullback started, it was up only about 7%.

    Recent findings suggest that the three cases that finished lower fell within around nine months of each other, in April 1999, July 1999, and January 2000. A year later, shares were down each time, by up to about 50%.

    The last one was by far the worst. Microsoft set a record close on Dec. 27, 1999, and fell 8% under it in January 2000. It didn't close above its 1999 high again until October 2016 -- almost 17 years later.

    According to recent reports, one big difference between then and now is valuation. In all three cases, the stock cost more than 60 times the earnings Microsoft had reported in the previous four quarters.

    Sources indicate that today, Microsoft's non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings for its past four quarters are $18.04 per share, a number that leaves out the impact of its investments in OpenAI. The stock trades at around 28 times those earnings.

    Recent findings suggest that true, the stock arguably still has a premium price for a tech business this big. But it's nowhere near the multiples investors paid then.

    Of course, earnings growth has cooled a little. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 18% year over year in Microsoft's fiscal first quarter of 2027 (the period ended Sept. 30, 2026). That was its slowest rate in at least four quarters, after growth between 21% and 24% in the previous three quarters.

    In a recent development, what makes this case unusual is that Microsoft's Nov. 4 record came on a one-day jump of almost 7%. None of the 18 past records in this study came on a one-day gain larger than about 5%.

    So a lot of the latest drop has just given that jump back. Measured from its Nov. 3 close of around $521, the stock is down only about 2%. In other words, the drop from the record likely overstates how much has changed for Microsoft since early November.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that all in all, the record here looks promising for long-term shareholders. A quick 8% slide from a high has usually been followed by gains, and the exceptions were when the stock was priced well above where it is now.

    But I don't see a reason to rush. More than half the time, buyers had a chance to pay at least 10% less at some point during the year.

    And with earnings growth slowing and the stock still about 28 times adjusted earnings, I'd rather wait for a lower price than the one offered now.

    If this pullback follows most of the others, that chance might come -- but history isn't a guarantee.

    • Sources indicate that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The debasement trade is gaining fresh traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

    Sources indicate that the conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

    "The size of the Treasury purchases unveiled so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," stated Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

    Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

    Industry observers note that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

    Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

    Industry observers note that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

    According to recent reports, the Treasury Department mentioned last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

    Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

    Long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

    Industry observers note that "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

    The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

    The stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah mentioned. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

    In a recent development, the Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah remarked. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

    "The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah stated in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

    Recent findings suggest that coltman at 21Shares said the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

    Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

    Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

    Recent findings suggest that billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

    It has been revealed that "The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

    It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, stated Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates dropped today, but anything above 7% still puts pressure on home buyers’ budgets.

    According to recent reports, the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.24% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 14 basis points lower than yesterday and three basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Recent findings suggest that A significant drop is eye-catching, but you should consider mortgage interest rates' overall direction, not just what's going on today. While the economy never sleeps, markets are closed on the weekends. The rates you see Friday are unlikely to change much (if at all) until Monday.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    According to recent reports, mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    Next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a major reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

    According to recent reports, if PCE shows inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

    According to recent reports, I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

    Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you strategy to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.74% or higher.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    If the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    In a recent development, nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a latest home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    Industry observers note that » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    Recent findings suggest that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

    Sources indicate that bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

    Just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side revealed some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

    Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    Stepping up in the major moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

    It has been revealed that aston Villa’s preparations for the latest season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

    After losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East.     Bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

    After today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

    By Dominic Basulto – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Hyperliquid ›.

    Industry observers note that one of the few bright spots in the crypto market has been Hyperliquid (HYPE +5.38%), up 140% for the year. Since its launch in late 2024, the HYPE token is up a remarkable 1,800%.

    Industry observers note that but can Hyperliquid hold on to these gains and surge even higher in the years ahead? If so, it could be a millionaire maker. But before you start shopping for luxury yachts and high-end vacation homes, here's what you need to know about Hyperliquid.

    In a recent development, first and foremost, Hyperliquid still faces tremendous regulatory obstacles. That's because Hyperliquid is a decentralized crypto exchange based offshore, and it doesn't yet have regulatory permission to operate in the U.S. or to offer its services to U.S. retail investors. If you try to trade on the Hyperliquid platform, you will immediately get a red warning message that you're in a restricted jurisdiction.

    Granted, President Donald Trump has given regulators the green light to bring Hyperliquid to the U.S. That's a huge positive. But the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) recently warned that Hyperliquid would be treated just like any other entity. Until it receives formal regulatory approval, Hyperliquid will need to partner with a registered exchange to offer financial derivatives to U.S. retail investors.

    Meanwhile, the number of participants lining up to offer perpetual futures -- the financial product that led to Hyperliquid's meteoric rise -- seems to increase by the day. That's because the CFTC gave the go-ahead for crypto perps in May and for equity perps in November, which has dramatically changed the competitive landscape.

    It's not just decentralized exchanges such as Hyperliquid that are potential rivals. Centralized crypto exchanges such as Coinbase Global (COIN -6.34%) and trading platforms like Robinhood Markets (HOOD -9.44%) are also potential rivals. So are prediction markets such as Kalshi and Polymarket. And what if legacy Wall Street financial exchanges decide to get into the act?

    Sources indicate that you get the idea. Competition could be off the charts, and that means Hyperliquid may start to account for a shrinking share of trading in perpetual futures. If that's the case, there's no way that it can grow at triple-digit percentage rates in coming years.

    According to recent reports, and here's the really scary fact: Hyperliquid is now down 37% from its all-time high of $97.98 in September. If roughly $100 were the top for HYPE, it wouldn't surprise me at all. In the crypto market, it's normal for highly volatile cryptos to skyrocket in price one year, only to collapse the next.

    All of this is to say: Don't believe the hype about HYPE.

    Given that almost all cryptocurrencies are down this year, it's easy to suspend disbelief and think that Hyperliquid might be a magic ticket to millionaire status. But I just don't think it has the staying power required to mint new millionaires. Hyperliquid might be beating the pants off Bitcoin (BTC +4.75%) this year, but I'd still rather buy Bitcoin.

    • Although some of Wall Street's most volatile single-session swings in history have occurred under President Donald Trump, few presidents since the late 1890s have overseen higher average annual stock market returns.
    • The stock market's list of catalysts under Trump is extensive and includes (but isn't limited to):.
    • Sources indicate that president Trump's bull market may be operating on borrowed time.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sean Williams – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:06AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Although some of Wall Street's most volatile single-session swings in history have occurred under President Donald Trump, few presidents since the late 1890s have overseen higher average annual stock market returns. During Trump's first term, the time-tested Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.93%), benchmark S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%), and innovation-powered Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) gained 57%, 70%, and 142%, respectively.

    The stock market's list of catalysts under Trump is extensive and includes (but isn't limited to):.

    Sources indicate that president Trump's bull market may be operating on borrowed time. Image source: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok.

    In a recent development, but things may not be as ideal for Wall Street as the major stock indexes have made them appear. History suggests the probability of a stock market crash occurring and driving the AI-driven Trump bull market notably lower is climbing by the day.

    Sources indicate that there's no argument that AI is the hottest trend on Wall Street since the advent and proliferation of the internet. Empowering software and systems to make autonomous decisions is a $22.5 trillion addressable opportunity through 2031, according to IDC, and it's the primary catalyst that's lifted the Trump bull market to upcoming heights.

    According to recent reports, but history also demonstrates that every next-massive-thing technology since (and including) the advent of the internet in the mid-1990s has navigated a bubble-bursting event. These bubbles repeatedly form and burst because investors persistently overestimate the pace of adoption and/or optimization of upcoming technologies.

    Stock market bubbles throughout history…AI stocks now ~40% of the market. pic.twitter.com/RxSAh09k6F.

    To be clear, AI doesn't have an adoption problem. The amount of capital being thrown around by neoclouds and hyperscalers shows that AI has been welcomed with open arms.

    However, the businesses deploying AI solutions aren't particularly close to optimizing them. It took until several years after the dot-com bubble burst for internet-driven companies to maximize this technology to boost their sales and profits, and we're likely looking at a similar timeline for AI, heightening the odds of a bubble-driven stock market crash.

    Premium stock valuations are another reason the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite could endure elevator-down moves in the presumed not-too-distant future.

    In a recent development, on the one hand, valuation is a tricky subject to tackle given that there isn't a one-size-fits-all way to evaluate individual companies or the broader market. Some combination of investor subjectivity and emotion leads to unpredictability on Wall Street.

    Stock Market Shiller PE Ratio on the verge of taking out its Dot Com Bubble all-time high 🚨 🤯 👀 pic.twitter.com/CtCmSgWnLt.

    It has been revealed that on the other hand, the S&P 500's Shiller Price-to-Earnings (P/E) Ratio, also known as the Cyclically Adjusted P/E Ratio (CAPE Ratio), is time-vetted and leaves little room for interpretation. The stock market entered this year at its second-highest valuation since January 1871 and only became more expensive throughout the summer.

    The S&P 500's CAPE Ratio has exceeded 30 only six times over 156 years, including the present, and the previous five instances were all eventually followed by declines of 20% to 89% in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500, and/or Nasdaq Composite. While the Shiller P/E Ratio doesn't tell investors when these downturns will begin or if a crash will occur, it does have a knack for foreshadowing substantial downside.

    Wall Street's crudest measure of investors' willingness to take risks also points to a heightened probability of a stock market crash.

    Recent findings suggest that every month, FINRA publishes the aggregated outstanding margin debt at all brokerages. Margin represents the money investors borrow, with interest, to short-sell or purchase securities. When it's used to buy stocks or exchange-traded funds, it acts as leverage.

    Recent findings suggest that investing on margin can be incredibly risky. It can magnify your gains if a security moves in the desired direction, but also rapidly amplify losses if it moves in the opposite direction.

    Total Margin Debt hits $1.5 Trillion, a upcoming all-time high 🤯 👀 pic.twitter.com/1IXqZGgrqs.

    According to recent reports, in June 2026, outstanding margin debt hit a record high of $1.502 trillion. While margin debt is expected to steadily climb with the overall stock market over time, parabolic moves higher over short time frames have historically been bad news. Between April 2025 and June 2026, margin debt soared 77%, marking the fourth time it's skyrocketed by at least 65% since 1998 over the span of just 12 to 19 months.

    Industry observers note that the prior three occurrences immediately preceded the bursting of the dot-com bubble in 2000, the start of the financial crisis in 2007, and the onset of the 2022 bear market. Some of these events featured crash-like moves.

    While none of these three history-backed events or metrics guarantee that a Trump bull market crash is imminent, the odds of a jaw-dropping downturn appear to be growing by the day.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1385 w)
