    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1385 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • According to recent reports, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's vital to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    According to recent reports, scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    It has been revealed that these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s notable to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    In a recent development, merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    Sources indicate that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that demonstrates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Sources indicate that even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Recent findings suggest that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    It has been revealed that scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    Which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    In a recent development, scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    In a recent development, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    According to recent reports, think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Recent findings suggest that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a significant impact when you add several of them together.

    Sources indicate that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    It has been revealed that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    But Eli Lilly also offers something that many of us associate with other industries, such as technology. I'm talking about growth. The organization has generated double-digit revenue gains in recent quarters thanks to its presence in the weight loss drug space. Lilly sells tirzepatide under the names Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes and Zepbound for weight loss. (Doctors have prescribed either one for the weight loss indication.).

    It has been revealed that all of this helped the stock climb more than 420% over the past five years, meaning that if you invested $1,000, you would have over $5,000 today. Could it soar that much again by 2031? Let's find out.

    It has been revealed that so, first, let's take a look at Eli Lilly's path over the past few years. This pharma giant sells a broad range of medicines across treatment areas, from cancer to migraine and Alzheimer's disease. But the area that has stood out in recent years is weight loss. Lilly's drugs are in the class known as GLP-1. These drugs act on hormonal pathways involved in digestion and therefore regulate appetite and blood sugar levels.

    Individuals aiming to lose weight have rushed to get in on GLP-1 drugs since they've proven safety and efficacy and are easy to self-administer. Mounjaro and Zepbound are weekly injections, and Lilly recently won approval for a newly introduced GLP-1 drug in pill format. That product is called Foundayo and may significantly broaden the audience for these types of drugs.

    Lilly isn't alone in the market; in fact, it wasn't even the leader in the early days of GLP-1 drugs. Novo Nordisk was the original leader, though Lilly slipped ahead in 2025. Now, the two are vying for leadership in the oral GLP-1 space, as Novo also rolled out an oral drug this year.

    Lilly's recent earnings report demonstrates the power of its GLP-1 drugs, with Mounjaro and Zepbound driving a 39% increase in revenue to more than $24 billion.

    The story doesn't end here, though. Lilly also has an extensive pipeline of weight loss drug candidates, including one called retatrutide that's in phase 3 studies and may have the potential to deliver greater weight loss. This could complement the existing portfolio, offering a variety of GLP-1 options for different needs.

    Industry observers note that now, let's consider whether an investment in Lilly could once again turn $1,000 into $5,000 over the coming five years. This would imply a gain of about 420%, taking the share price to about $7,092 -- and the market cap from $1.2 trillion today to $6.3 trillion. This surpasses the value of today's biggest technology leaders.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that of course, it's possible that over the coming five years, tech players also will gain, seeing their market values march higher. So the market as a whole may see value climb significantly, making the Lilly jump to more than $6 trillion seem less shocking.

    In a recent development, that noted, after the S&P 500's 78% increase over the past three calendar years and the double- and triple-digit gains of many substantial stocks, I wouldn't count on the same momentum over the coming five years -- for the general market or for Lilly. This doesn't mean the market or Lilly will drop. I think there's still potential for gains, and Lilly's weight loss portfolio and potentially new releases from the pipeline could drive significant growth.

    Though I would be surprised to see another gain of 400%, I think it's possible to see a double- or triple-digit increase from Lilly stock over the next five years -- and that means I consider it a great buy today.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that if you're enrolled in Medicare, there's an important deadline approaching that could affect how much you pay for healthcare next year.
    • Recent findings suggest that even if you're satisfied with your current Medicare initiative, assuming everything will remain the same and there's no better option out there could be a costly mistake.
    • In a recent development, open enrollment gives you an opportunity to make changes to your Medicare coverage.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Maurie Backman – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:18AM EST.

    Recent findings suggest that if you're enrolled in Medicare, there's an important deadline approaching that could affect how much you pay for healthcare next year. Medicare's fall open enrollment period ends on Dec. 7. That means you only have a limited amount of time to review your coverage and make changes for 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that even if you're satisfied with your current Medicare initiative, assuming everything will remain the same and there's no better option out there could be a costly mistake. So make sure to do these three things before the Dec. 7 deadline arrives.

    In a recent development, open enrollment gives you an opportunity to make changes to your Medicare coverage. But before you can decide whether a new plan is best, you have to understand what's happening with your current one.

    Recent findings suggest that to that end, if you haven't reviewed your current plan's annual notice of change, now's the time to read through it thoroughly. That notice should explain any upcoming changes to things like premiums, deductibles, copays, covered services, and other benefits.

    Recent findings suggest that don't just skim that document, though. Even a relatively small monthly premium increase could add up over the course of a year. And if your Medicare Advantage proposal is dropping benefits, that could have a huge impact on you, too.

    Recent findings suggest that before comparing Medicare aims, take the time to make a list of every prescription medication you currently take. Include the medication's name, dosage, how frequently you take it, and the pharmacy you typically use for refills.

    Industry observers note that this step is important because Medicare Part D plans can change their drug formularies, which are lists of covered prescription medications, from one year to the next. A medication covered by your current strategy might be moved to a different cost-sharing tier in 2027, making it more expensive. Having a comprehensive list should make it easier to compare plans and determine which one offers the best coverage for your specific medications.

    Even if your current Medicare strategy isn't changing for the worse, you shouldn't assume that it's your best option for next year. There may be another plan that offers lower premiums and prescription drug costs.

    If you've been diagnosed with any newly introduced conditions over the past year, it also pays to see if there's a Medicare Advantage plan offering supplemental benefits that could help you manage it better. Medicare Advantage plans commonly offer added benefits beyond what original Medicare covers.

    Recent findings suggest that it might seem like you have plenty of time to take action on your Medicare coverage before Dec. 7 rolls around. But that deadline will be here before you know it. So if you haven't yet reviewed changes to your current Medicare initiative, your prescription list, and new plan options, the time to get moving is now.

    Industry observers note that this estimate hinges on one earnings path, based mainly on Broadcom's artificial intelligence (AI) chips, and one ending valuation. It also comes before the manufacturer's fiscal fourth-quarter report on Dec. 9, which might change both.

    And it relies most on one assumption: that a really short list of customers keeps buying.

    Industry observers note that showing how fast the AI business is scaling, Broadcom's AI semiconductor revenue climbed 221% year over year to $16.7 billion in the fiscal third quarter of 2026 (the period ended Aug. 2, 2026). Management sees fiscal Q4 AI revenue of $21.7 billion, an acceleration to 236% growth, which would take the fiscal 2026 total to about $58 billion. Custom AI chips, which Broadcom designs for specific customers, made up 73% of the third-quarter total. And AI networking revenue, from the chips that tie those processors together, climbed over 2.5-fold from a year earlier.

    Management also stated on its September earnings call that it's locked in the supply to double AI revenue again in fiscal 2027, to about $115 billion. It sees a path to $230 billion in fiscal 2028, and it expects networking to grow just as fast as the custom chips.

    "As a result, I got to say we are very much on target to exceed $30 in earnings per share in fiscal 2028," CEO Hock Tan said on the call.

    I use that $30 as my base for fiscal 2028. Then, I assume earnings growth slows to around 10% a year as the largest data center build-outs mature. This would put earnings per share at about $40 in fiscal 2031.

    Today, the stock price is around 18 times the fiscal 2027 earnings per share analysts expect on average. The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) traded at about 18 times forward earnings in mid-November, according to FactSet.

    Sure, Broadcom is growing far faster than the index now. By the end of 2030, though, investors will probably be pricing the stock on fiscal 2031 earnings, and growth should be much slower. So I assume a lower price-to-earnings ratio of around 15.

    At 15 times forward earnings of about $40, the stock would be worth about $600.

    That means all the gain in my estimate comes from earnings growth, with investors paying less for every dollar of Broadcom's profit than they do now.

    According to recent reports, profitability looks like a smaller risk. Management expects adjusted gross margin to ease to around 73% in fiscal Q4, from 78% a year earlier, as memory-heavy custom chips grow. But it sees the adjusted operating margin staying at about 66%, flat year over year.

    The bigger risk is who buys those chips. Broadcom estimates that its top five end customers made up around 55% of its fiscal third-quarter revenue, versus about 40% a year earlier. In the first three quarters of fiscal 2026, that share was about 50%.

    It has been revealed that broadcom makes custom AI chips for six customers. Management expects Anthropic to become the largest of them in 2027, and OpenAI the second largest in 2028.

    The company's latest quarterly filing warns that losing any top-five customer, or a major fall in demand from one, could have a material adverse effect on its business.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    What if the major deployments are around two years late? Then earnings per share might hit $30 in fiscal 2030 and about $33 in fiscal 2031. At the same 15 times forward earnings, the stock would land near $500 instead, for yearly gains of about 9%.

    Recent findings suggest that that's still a decent return. But a customer that stops buying entirely could do much more harm.

    All in all, I think around $600 is a fair estimate for Broadcom stock at the end of 2030. If those customers keep building, today's price looks reasonable to me for a organization with that path ahead of it. But that's just a guess, and much of it rests on spending decisions Broadcom doesn't control.

    Latest Update: I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1642 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
    • Recent findings suggest that take Southwest Airlines, for example.
    • "Experiences create lifetime memories,” says Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

    Recent findings suggest that take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

    "Experiences create lifetime memories,” says Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

    Southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

    Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but big-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

    The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

    In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

    A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

    Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

    A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

    A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

    A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

    Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

    As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

    Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

    $1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

    Four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

    It has been revealed that if you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

    In a recent development, using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

    It has been revealed that daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

    Ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

    Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

    I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

    Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

    Sources indicate that again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

    Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

    It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

    I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

    Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

    Grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

    It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

    Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

    According to recent reports, the biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

    It has been revealed that you’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

    According to recent reports, with that stated, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

    These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

    Sources indicate that scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

    It has been revealed that finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

    Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

    But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

    According to recent reports, personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

    Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

    "We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” indicates Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

    If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

    Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

    Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

    According to recent reports, you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s crucial to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    Latest Update: The Stock Market Sounds an Alarm as Investors Get Bad News About President Donald Trump's Economy

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) delivered positive returns for much of 2026, supported by strong corporate earnings and enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence.
    • Unfortunately, the situation could get worse.
    • President Donald Trump sits with his hands clasped during a meeting at the White House, surrounded by administration officials.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Trevor Jennewine – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:21AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    Industry observers note that the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) and Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) delivered positive returns for much of 2026, supported by strong corporate earnings and enthusiasm surrounding artificial intelligence. But both indexes recently entered market correction territory, falling more than 10% from their respective highs.

    Unfortunately, the situation could get worse. Investors recently received troubling updates about President Donald Trump's economy: Inflation accelerated in September, and subsequent estimates suggest pricing pressures have continued to intensify. Meanwhile, the stock market is sounding an alarm last seen during the dot-com bubble.

    Here's what investors should know.

    President Donald Trump sits with his hands clasped during a meeting at the White House, surrounded by administration officials. Image source: Official White House Photo.

    Sources indicate that inflation accelerated in September, complicating the Federal Reserve's effort to restore price stability. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) increased 3.7% from the previous year, up from 3.4% in August and the highest reading since May.

    Industry observers note that research from the Federal Reserve Banks of St. Louis and Minneapolis helps explain why prices are rising more swiftly. President Trump's tariffs were the primary driver of inflation earlier in the year, but supply shocks driven by energy sector prices have since become the primary culprit. The Iran war has disrupted Middle Eastern oil shipments, pushing crude oil prices and transportation costs higher.

    Unfortunately, the inflation outlook remains troubling. The Cleveland Fed estimates that headline CPI inflation is trending toward 3.9% in November. And core CPI inflation (which excludes volatile food and energy prices) is projected to accelerate to 2.9%, up from 2.6% in September, suggesting that elevated energy prices are spreading to other areas of the economy.

    Sources indicate that the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate in September, the first rate hike in three years, but investors expect another rate hike in December due to persistent inflation. That bodes ill for the stock market because higher interest rates increase borrowing costs for consumers and businesses, potentially slowing economic growth and creating a drag on corporate profits. They also make bonds more attractive relative to stocks, which can put downward pressure on equity valuations.

    In a recent development, the price-to-earnings (PE) ratio is one of the most widely used equity valuation metrics. It divides a company's share price by its earnings per share from the last 12 months. But the cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio takes a different approach, dividing the inflation-adjusted price by the average inflation-adjusted earnings from the last decade. That methodology smooths fluctuations in corporate profits caused by the business cycle.

    In a recent development, the S&P 500's CAPE ratio was 40.1 in October, marking the sixth straight monthly reading above 40. Previously, the index's CAPE ratio last exceeded 40 during the dot-com crash in September 2000. Unfortunately, such rich valuations have often preceded dismal returns, as shown in the table below.

    Data source: Robert Shiller, YCharts.

    Historically, following months in which the S&P 500's CAPE ratio exceeded 40, the index returned an average of 0% over the next six months; it declined by an average of 3% over the next year; and it declined by an average of 19% over the next two years. In other words, history suggests the stock market is headed much lower.

    However, one limitation of the CAPE ratio is its backward-looking nature. It does not incorporate forward earnings estimates, meaning it may overstate valuations when corporate profits are growing rapidly. Artificial intelligence has already contributed to higher profit margins and higher earnings growth across the S&P 500, and that trend is projected to continue.

    Additionally, the historical returns shown in the table reflect overlapping periods during the dot-com bubble, rather than numerous independent market episodes. Consequently, they illustrate the risks associated with extreme valuations, but do not definitively predict what will happen next.

    Industry observers note that nevertheless, investors should not dismiss this warning entirely The stock market remains expensive by historical standards, and the prospect of higher interest rates could put additional pressure on valuations. Together, those headwinds could push the S&P 500 into a bear market. If that happens, remember that dips have historically been great buying opportunities: The S&P 500 has rebounded from every past drawdown.

    Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

    The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

    Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge before beginning their Premier League campaign at Fulham.

    AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    Chelsea take on Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia tomorrow before returning to the UK. Their final pre-season game will be against Real Sociedad before taking on Fulham on the opening weekend of the upcoming season.

    AC Milan will play Manchester United next weekend and then kick off their Serie A campaign against Torino.

Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

    It has been revealed that yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

    Chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have new managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

    Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

    In a recent development, “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so key to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

    It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

    AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their substantial-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

    Where Will Micron Stock Be in 3 Years?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost nearly half its market cap in five months.
    • Sources indicate that wall Street thinks that Micron has a lot of room to run.
    • In a recent development, the bull case for Micron is that its stock soars to between $1,800 and $2,200 by late 2029, a gain of 3.2x at the midpoint of the range.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keith Speights – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:26AM EST.

    Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) has lost nearly half its market cap in five months. That's the bad news. The good news is that the semiconductor stock is still up nearly 120% year-to-date.

    Sources indicate that wall Street thinks that Micron has a lot of room to run. The consensus 12-month price target reflects a potential upside of around 160%. But where will Micron stock be in three years? There are three potential scenarios.

    In a recent development, the bull case for Micron is that its stock soars to between $1,800 and $2,200 by late 2029, a gain of 3.2x at the midpoint of the range. To make this scenario possible, the demand for the tech giant's memory chips would need to remain strong over the next several years. In addition, the humanoid robot market would need to gain momentum. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said in the company's fiscal 2026 third-quarter earnings call that he expects a "sustained, substantial multi-decade memory demand cycle" to begin later this decade.

    The base case is that the stock jumps to $1,100 to $1,400. Micron's share price would roughly double at the midpoint of this range. The high-bandwidth memory (HBM) market would need to continue growing robustly in this scenario. It also assumes that Chinese memory chip manufacturer ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) gains only modest market share with its HBM chips. However, Micron probably wouldn't require the humanoid robot market to pick up significant steam for the base case to be achieved.

    In a recent development, what's the bear case? Micron's stock declines to a range of $400 to $600 over the next three years. The most likely way this scenario could unfold is if CXMT advances its HBM technology faster than expected and changes the market dynamics. An influx of HBM supply could trigger a price war among major HBM suppliers. As Micron's margins fall, so would its share price. A slowdown in AI infrastructure spending could also weigh on Micron's stock. With many investors already nervous about hyperscalers' massive AI-related capital expenditures and a growing public backlash against AI data centers in the U.S., such a slowdown isn't out of the question.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, micron is still a cyclical stock. Any of the three scenarios is possible, depending on the duration and intensity of the current memory chip boom. That stated, if I had to predict where Micron stock will actually be three years from now, it would be around the lower end of the base-case range.

    Sources indicate that I fully expect the demand for HBM to remain strong. Whether the humanoid robot market becomes a significant tailwind for Micron between now and 2029 remains to be seen, though. As for CXMT, I think the company will be a key player in HBM. However, I don't anticipate that Micron's growth will be derailed because of increased competition. A cumulative gain of 80% or more for Micron over the next three years seems attainable, in my view.

    Top Wall Street analysts find these 3 stocks attractive as long-term investments

    📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (937 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety.
    • Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure tech giant Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    It has been revealed that after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he said.

    It has been revealed that "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," noted DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as fresh contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    Sources indicate that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space organization with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (668 w)

    What Every 60-Year-Old Should Know About Social Security

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (668 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that I suspect that nearly every American who is 60 is already thinking about retirement -- as they should.
    • There's still plenty of time to finalize those decisions, but it's not too soon to begin thinking about them.
    • Recent findings suggest that no Social Security decision is more important than choosing when you claim benefits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Keith Speights – Nov 22, 2026 at 4:44AM EST.

    Recent findings suggest that I suspect that nearly every American who is 60 is already thinking about retirement -- as they should. And that involves contemplating upcoming decisions about Social Security. Making the right choices can have lifelong implications.

    There's still plenty of time to finalize those decisions, but it's not too soon to begin thinking about them. Here are five things every 60-year-old should know about Social Security.

    Recent findings suggest that no Social Security decision is more important than choosing when you claim benefits. If you're 60, you could file for benefits within the next two years. However, make sure you understand the trade-offs of claiming before your full retirement age (FRA) of 67.

    The Social Security Administration (SSA) will reduce benefits by around 30% for anyone who claims at age 62. And the early-retirement penalty is permanent. Your benefits will only increase with annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs). On the other hand, holding off until age 70 to claim Social Security will increase your benefits by 24% compared with claiming at 67.

    Many people will decide the advantages of claiming at 62 are worth forgoing the higher monthly benefits. That's especially true for those who don't expect to live past their late 70s. There isn't a one-size-fits-all right decision. Every person needs to fully consider all factors for their personal situation.

    Putting aside the early-retirement penalties and delayed-retirement credits, working longer could increase your Social Security benefit for another reason. SSA calculates your benefit using the 35 years with your highest earnings, adjusted for inflation. Many earn significantly more in the last few years of their careers than they did early on. Those higher-earnings years can replace the lower-earnings ones and boost your Social Security benefit.

    This is even more crucial for anyone with fewer than 35 years of earnings. If you don't have at least a 35-year earnings record, SSA will plug zeros in for the missing years in its benefits calculation.

    If you spot a potential problem, check with SSA about what supporting documentation you'll need to get it fixed. Getting your earnings record correct at age 60 could spare you major headaches later after you claim benefits.

    Don't think that the decisions you make about Social Security only impact you. They can also affect your spouse.

    For example, the higher-earning spouse's claiming age permanently sets the survivor benefits available to the other spouse if the higher-earning spouse dies first. Coordinating when each spouse claims Social Security benefits is an vital step that shouldn't be overlooked.

    Benjamin Franklin wrote that "nothing can be stated to be certain, except death and taxes." Unfortunately, his statement is still applicable -- even for Social Security benefits, in some cases.

    Up to 85% of your Social Security benefits could be subject to federal income taxes depending on your combined income, which is calculated by summing your adjusted gross income, nontaxable interest, and half of your Social Security benefits. The thresholds where federal taxes begin to kick in are $25,000 for single filers and $32,000 for married couples.

    Right now, 42 states plus the District of Columbia don't tax Social Security benefits. However, if you live in Colorado, Connecticut, Minnesota, Montana, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Utah, or Vermont, some of your Social Security income may be subject to tax.

    According to recent reports, the good news if you're 60 is that you don't have to make any Social Security decisions immediately. The bad news is that time flies. Starting to think about retirement and Social Security now could pay off later.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
    • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
    • According to recent reports, you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The significant day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

    If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

    According to recent reports, you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

    If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, says Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

    Non-electronic toys are a good bet, indicates Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

    NeeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold indicates.

    While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

    Sources indicate that “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” notes Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

    Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley states.

    Got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

    Industry observers note that “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath indicates. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

    Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

    While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold notes.

    According to recent reports, electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath claims.

    Gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

    That noted, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold says.

    For best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, says consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

    You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after New Year’s Day.

    “Substantial-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold indicates.

    It has been revealed that many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath claims. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

    Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold claims. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

    Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

    According to recent reports, one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch claims. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

    Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

    Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

    In a recent development, fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch indicates.

    Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

    Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

    Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

    In a recent development, let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch says. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

    Check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

    Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    • Last month, Tesla (TSLA -7.64%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) each formed a special committee of independent directors to consider a merger.
    • A deal would combine the top space tech giant and automaker by market cap.
    • Although both companies are richly valued, SpaceX stock has the higher market cap and valuation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Lyle Daly – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tesla ›.

    Last month, Tesla (TSLA -7.64%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -7.69%) each formed a special committee of independent directors to consider a merger. Elon Musk, the CEO and largest individual shareholder of both companies, can't participate in the talks.

    A deal would combine the top space tech giant and automaker by market cap. For Tesla investors, the biggest change may be how the market values the company's robotaxi business.

    Although both companies are richly valued, SpaceX stock has the higher market cap and valuation. It's worth $2 trillion and trades at 58 times trailing sales, as of Nov. 19. Tesla has a market cap of $1.5 trillion and trades at 13 times trailing sales.

    Tesla's valuation is largely tied to humanoid robots, robotaxis, and AI services such as full self-driving (FSD). But cars are still the core business, and Tesla's operating income declined 56% year over year to $718 million in Q3 2026. Currently, robotaxi is part of a car company, which weighs on how the market can value it.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that A merger would put robotaxi inside a manufacturer with a rapidly growing AI business, with revenue that skyrocketed 830% year over year to $7.6 billion in Q3. Investors could start valuing it as an AI business, not an add-on to a car business.

    Recent findings suggest that robotaxi is an expensive business that requires vehicles, chips, compute resources, and connectivity. Tesla's network is also expanding quickly, with nearly 2 million cumulative unsupervised miles logged by the end of September, growing about eightfold from the previous quarter. As the network grows, costs will continue to increase.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that spaceX is spending heavily on AI, reporting $48.1 billion in capital expenditures over the first nine months of 2026. It's guiding for another $35 billion to $40 billion in Q4. Tesla is pulling back, revising its capex guidance down to about $20 billion in 2026, from more than $25 billion. SpaceX could provide the robotaxi business with more funding, its existing AI infrastructure, and connectivity through the Starlink network, all contributing to faster expansion.

    Although robotaxi is an exciting business, it's not yet making a financial impact. Musk doesn't expect it to make a noticeable difference to Tesla's finances until around Q2 2027, and that may be an optimistic viewpoint. He previously expected robotaxi service to be widespread across the U.S. by the end of 2026. Tesla offers service in nine metro areas, so it's a long way to go, showing how reality often falls well short of expectations.

    Recent findings suggest that if there's a merger, robotaxi will become part of a company potentially worth $3.5 trillion or more. Investors could have a harder time tracking robotaxi's progress than they do now.

    Merger talks are in the early stages, with no proposed terms. Tesla would also need approval from a majority of all outstanding shares, not just those voting, because Musk doesn't control the company's voting power as he does with SpaceX. A merger could make robotaxi a more valuable business, but for now, what's important is that it starts producing meaningful revenue in 2027.

    Sources indicate that when Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park.     Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

    Yesterday Arsenal confirmed the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:.

    “I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a latest challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”.

    Industry observers note that premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the latest season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    According to recent reports, arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    Sources indicate that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    Recent findings suggest that “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    In a recent development, dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

    10 stocks we like better than ASML ›.

    Sources indicate that nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) delivered incredible results for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended on Oct. 25) and, more importantly, raised its revenue guidance for fiscal 2028.

    Nvidia's financial performance and outlook should come as a relief for investors during a difficult time. The firm's co-founder Jensen Huang recently resigned as CEO, and Nvidia is now in the hunt for a latest one. However, comments from interim CEO Colette Kress on the latest earnings call clearly suggest that the company's growth prospects remain solid.

    Nvidia's revenue increased by 103% year-over-year last quarter to $115.8 billion, driven by a 110% jump in data center revenue. The organization anticipates $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter, an improvement of 91% over the year-ago quarter. Even better, Nvidia has raised its fiscal 2028 revenue guidance to 75%, up from the prior expectation of 70%.

    So, I won't be surprised to see this artificial intelligence (AI) specialist go on a bull run once again. But if you're still on the sidelines about Nvidia's prospects, it may be a good idea to take a closer look at another semiconductor stock -- ASML Holding (ASML -6.63%). Here's why.

    Sources indicate that nvidia's impressive data center growth in the previous quarter was driven by the incredible demand for its latest-generation Vera Rubin chip systems. The firm noted that the Vera Rubin platform generated almost $20 billion in revenue last quarter, "making it the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history.".

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer noted that Rubin deployments will continue improving in 2027. Moreover, Nvidia management remarked that demand for its chips is outpacing supply. All this bodes well for ASML Holding, which manufactures the advanced chipmaking equipment that enables Nvidia to make the advanced Blackwell and Vera Rubin processors.

    Nvidia's Vera Rubin chip is built on a 3-nanometer (nm) process node, while the previous-generation Blackwell architecture, which remains in solid demand, is built on a 4-nm process node. These small process nodes are manufactured using extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, and ASML holds a near monopoly in this market.

    In a recent development, not surprisingly, ASML has seen a significant increase in demand for its lithography machines. The company sold 113 fresh lithography systems in the third quarter of 2026, up from 66 in the year-ago period. As demand for advanced AI chips exceeds supply, ASML is looking to increase the production capacity of its EUV lithography machines.

    The company aims to increase the production of machines that make advanced chips by 30% in 2027. What's more, it is exploring the possibility of enhancing capacity by more than 30% in 2028. ASML management noted on the October earnings call:.

    So, ASML seems well-positioned to sustain solid long-term growth, and what makes it a better investment than Nvidia is the fact that multiple foundries and memory manufacturers use its machines.

    ASML's customer base includes Nvidia's foundry partner, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, Samsung, Intel, and Micron Technology, among others. This diversified customer base means that ASML stands to gain from both the foundry/logic and memory markets, making it a safer bet than Nvidia.

    Additionally, ASML is now growing at a nice clip, driven by the increasing demand for its EUV machines.

    ASML Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts.

    Analysts are forecasting a 68% increase in ASML's earnings in 2026, followed by solid double-digit increases over the next couple of years.

    ASML EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts.

    If ASML's earnings reach $85.68 per share in 2028 and it trades at 30 times earnings, in line with the tech-laden Nasdaq-100 index's earnings multiple, its stock price could reach $2,570. That implies a potential upside of 78%. So, investors looking to avoid the uncertainty surrounding Nvidia can consider investing in ASML, as it trades at an attractive 22 times forward earnings and is likely to deliver steady gains over the next couple of years.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that MPLX (MPLX -1.27%), a midstream company spun off from Marathon Petroleum (MPC -0.20%) in 2012, operates over 10,000 miles of crude oil and light-product pipelines in 14 states.
    • MPLX is a master limited partnership (MLP) that passes its taxable income through to investors rather than paying federal corporate income tax.
    • MLPs cover their distributions (not dividends) with their distributable cash flow (DCF).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Leo Sun – Nov 22, 2026 at 5:07AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than MPLX ›.

    Sources indicate that MPLX (MPLX -1.27%), a midstream company spun off from Marathon Petroleum (MPC -0.20%) in 2012, operates over 10,000 miles of crude oil and light-product pipelines in 14 states. It pays a forward yield of 8.9%, and it's raised its annual payout by 12.5% for three consecutive years.

    MPLX is a master limited partnership (MLP) that passes its taxable income through to investors rather than paying federal corporate income tax. These distributions are often treated in part as a return of capital, which reduces an investor's cost basis and defers their taxes until the position is sold. That structure can be more tax-efficient than earning dividends from traditional corporations, but it requires investors to report an additional K-1 tax form every year.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    MLPs cover their distributions (not dividends) with their distributable cash flow (DCF). MPLX spent 64%, 65.3%, and 71.5% of its annualized DCF on distributions in 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively. That ratio declined as it ramped up its investments and acquisitions in 2025, but it can probably still afford to raise its annual distributions for at least the next few years.

    According to recent reports, MPLX has already generated a total return of 179% over the past five years, but it could still have more upside potential if oil prices stay elevated and its pipeline volumes hold steady. It's well-insulated from volatile oil prices -- since it merely charges companies "tolls" to use its infrastructure -- and it should remain a reliable income play for the foreseeable future.

    Solana Just Introduced New Privacy Features. Is It Worth Buying With $500 Right Now?
